title: I know you're busy, but I just need to complain about you doing your job
author: Andrew Old
summary: This article examines how technology has transformed parent-teacher communication and its impact on school discipline systems. Andrew Old argues that while teachers have historically dealt with unreasonable parents and complaints, technology—particularly real-time messaging through school portals—has fundamentally changed the frequency and manner of this communication. Schools now notify parents immediately of every decision, from behavior points to merits, often even reporting when children leave class for the restroom. This constant real-time feedback and direct messaging ability is affecting schools' discipline systems, as teachers face immediate parental challenges to their professional decisions. The article explores how this technology-enabled transparency, while well-intentioned, creates new dynamics that undermine teacher authority and classroom management.
points: Technology has transformed parent-teacher communication from occasional letters to real-time notifications about every classroom decision, creating constant parental scrutiny. Immediate notification of minor decisions invites immediate parental questioning of professional judgment, undermining teacher authority and classroom discipline. Direct messaging portals allow parents to challenge teachers instantly, affecting teachers' ability to maintain authority and manage classroom behavior consistently. The constant feedback loop created by technology encourages helicopter parenting and second-guessing of professional educators' decisions. Schools must balance transparency with protecting teacher professional autonomy and authority to maintain effective discipline systems.
quotes: For a very long time, teachers had to deal with unreasonable parents.
Technology has transformed the manner and frequency of communication between parents and teachers.
Almost every decision a teacher makes can now be transmitted straight to parents via the internet.
Some schools even let parents know every time their child leaves a lesson.
